newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pace of yen correction too rapid -- BOJ official.
newsitem.headline: Pace of yen correction too rapid -- BOJ official.

text.p: The correction to the yen's weakness has started, but the pace has been too rapid, a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television broadcast on Thursday.

"Correction to the yen's excessive weakness has begun, but the pace has been too rapid," Takashi Anzai, executive director of the BOJ, said. "The market is in the process of finding the (yen) exchange levels that reflect fundamentals. We hope to see it (the yen's exchange rate) stabilise as soon as possible."
He also said that Japan's economy is getting on to a recovery track.
Anzai added that the uncertainties about Japan's financial system had now passed their peak.
"Those factors have been priced in the recent market movements in stocks and bonds. This in turn prompted corrections to the overly devalued yen," Anzai said.
Japan's economy has been more dependent on domestic than external factors, he said.

"If any problem, such as slow import growth, arises as a result of policy geared to domestic factors, that should be dealt with by such measures as deregulation, rather than through macro-economic policies," he said.
